privacy.contact-body: Open an issue on the project's GitHub repository: {{url}}
privacy.control-body: Export or delete any child's data any time, from Backup and from that child's Settings in the parent area.
privacy.data-body: A nickname, an avatar picture, and lesson progress for each child — stored only on this device, never sent anywhere.
privacy.intro: {{app}} keeps everything on this device. Here's exactly what that means.
privacy.network-body: The only network access is checking for app updates. Updates are static files delivered from GitHub Pages. "Send to other device" hands the file to whichever app or device the parent picks — the app itself still sends nothing.
privacy.no-accounts-body: No sign-up, no analytics, no ads, no third-party services. The app never phones home.

bugs.drop-zero: An empty place still needs a zero to hold its spot.
bugs.five-down: Right in the middle? It goes up to the bigger number.
bugs.forgot-adjust: You used the round number. Now fix the answer by 1.
bugs.halve-tens-only: Halve the tens and the ones.
bugs.neighbour: So close, just one off! Count again.
bugs.off-by-one: So close! Count the last jump again.
bugs.swap: Look at the order: hundreds, then tens, then ones.
bugs.tens-only: Double the tens and the ones.
bugs.ticks-not-gaps: Count the jumps between the marks, not the marks.
bugs.truncate: Rounding down every time? Check which number is nearer.
bugs.wrong-op: Read it again: does the number get bigger or smaller?
bugs.wrong-place: Ten changes the tens digit. A hundred changes the hundreds digit.

market-orders.title: Market Orders

mm-bonds.demo: Look: 64 plus what makes 100? The tens: 6 and 3 make 90. The ones: 4 and 6 make 10. So 36 goes in the gap!
mm-bonds.story: Owl says: number bonds are pairs that make a round number. Hedgie knows 6 and 4 make 10, so 60 and 40 make 100. Find the partner and fill the gap!
mm-bonds.title: Number bonds

mm-bridge.demo: Look: 38 plus 7. Make a ten first: 2 more makes 40. Then 5 are left, so 40 plus 5 is 45!
mm-bridge.story: Owl says: a ten is a bridge. Hedgie makes a ten first, then adds what is left. To count up, jump to the next ten and then on!
mm-bridge.title: Bridge through ten

mm-doubles.demo: Look: 35 plus 36. Double 35 is 70, and 36 is one more than 35, so the answer is 71!
mm-doubles.story: Owl says: a double adds a number to itself, and half is one of two equal parts. Hedgie uses doubles to help: 35 plus 36 is double 35 and 1 more. To halve, split the tens and the ones!
mm-doubles.title: Doubles and halves

mm-problems.demo: Look: Fox has 12 berries and finds 5 more. The berries come together, so add. 12 plus 5 makes 17!
mm-problems.story: Owl says: read the story, then ask what is happening. Hedgie adds when parts come together and takes away when some go. How many more compares two numbers: take the smaller from the larger!
mm-problems.title: Story problems

mm-tens.demo: Look: 46 plus 99. Add 100 to get 146. But 99 is 1 less than 100, so take 1 away: 145!
mm-tens.story: Owl says: adding 10 changes only the tens digit, and adding 100 only the hundreds digit. Hedgie uses round numbers for the nearly ones, because 99 is 100 less 1. Add the round number, then fix the 1!
mm-tens.title: Tens, hundreds, nearly

mt-2-5-10.demo: What is 5 times 6? Count by 5, six times: 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30. So 5 times 6 is 30!
mt-2-5-10.story: Owl says: some times tables are easy to skip count. Hedgie counts by 2s, by 5s and by 10s. Count along, and the answer appears!
mt-2-5-10.title: Twos, fives, tens

mt-3-6-9.demo: What is 9 times 4? 10 times 4 is 40, and one 4 less is 36. So 9 times 4 is 36!
mt-3-6-9.story: Owl says: 6 is double 3, and 9 is one less than 10. Hedgie counts by 3s, doubles them for the 6s, and takes one group away from the 10s for the 9s!
mt-3-6-9.title: Threes, sixes, nines

mt-4-8.demo: What is 4 times 3? Double 3 makes 6, and double 6 makes 12. So 4 times 3 is 12!
mt-4-8.story: Owl says: to times by 4, double the number, then double it again. Hedgie knows that 8 is double 4, so for eights double one more time!
mt-4-8.title: Fours and eights

mt-7-mixed.demo: What is 7 times 6? 5 times 7 is 35, and one more 7 makes 42. So 7 times 6 is 42!
mt-7-mixed.story: Owl says: the 7s are the trickiest, and you already know most of them! Hedgie has two tricks: anything times 0 is 0, and anything times 1 stays the same.
mt-7-mixed.title: Sevens and mixed

mt-arrays.demo: This array has 3 rows of 4 dots. 4 plus 4 plus 4 makes 12, so 3 times 4 is 12. Turn it round, and 4 times 3 is 12 too!
mt-arrays.story: Owl says: an array is dots in rows, with the same number of dots in every row. Hedgie counts the rows, then the dots in one row. Rows go across!
mt-arrays.title: Arrays

mt-groups.demo: Look: 3 groups of 4 berries. 4 plus 4 plus 4 makes 12. So 3 times 4 is 12!
mt-groups.story: Owl says: times is a short way to talk about equal groups. Hedgie has 3 groups with 4 berries in each. Add 4 three times, and the berries are easy to count!
mt-groups.title: Equal groups

number-train.goal: Put every carriage number where it belongs on the line!
number-train.title: Number Train

pv-compare.demo: Compare 406 and 460. The hundreds are the same, so look at the tens. 0 tens is less than 6 tens, so 406 is smaller!
pv-compare.story: Owl says: look at the biggest place first. Hedgie checks the hundreds, then the tens. The open side of the sign faces the bigger number!
pv-compare.title: Bigger or smaller?

pv-hto.demo: Look: 2 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones. The zero holds the tens place, so the number is 205!
pv-hto.story: Owl says: every digit has a place. Hedgie counts the hundreds, then the tens, then the ones. An empty place still needs a zero!
pv-hto.title: Hundreds, tens, ones

pv-line.demo: This line goes from 0 to 1000, with a mark every 100. To find 300, Hedgie counts three jumps from 0!
pv-line.story: Owl says: a number line is a path of numbers. Every jump is the same size. Hedgie counts the jumps, not the marks!
pv-line.title: The number line

pv-round.demo: Round 47 to the nearest ten. The ones digit is 7, so go up. 47 is closer to 50 than to 40!
pv-round.story: Owl says: rounding finds the nearest ten or hundred. Hedgie checks the next digit: 5 or more goes up, less than 5 stays down.
pv-round.title: Rounding

pv-thousands.demo: Look: 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones. The zero keeps the tens place, so the number is 3405!
pv-thousands.story: Owl says: ten hundreds make one thousand. The thousands get a place on the left. Hedgie reads thousands, hundreds, tens, then ones!
pv-thousands.title: Thousands

race-to-20.goal: Take turns adding 1, 2 or 3. Whoever says 20 wins!
race-to-20.title: Race to 20
